Promoting small airlines and seaplanes, and easing traffic in Phuket
se: The meeting considered ways to promote small aircraft and seaplanes, to make use of regional airports and link main cities with secondary cities, with aircraft of about 7–15 seats serving as connecting airlines to support tourism and local economies. Operators described problems such as landing fees and ground handling charges that do not fit the size of the aircraft, in some places up to 30,000 baht per flight; legal limits on using some kinds of airfields; permits for water aerodromes involving many agencies; a shortage of experienced pilots; and the opening hours of regional airports. The Border Patrol Police Bureau presented the use of drones (UAV) to carry supplies to remote areas. The meeting proposed adjusting fees and ground charges for aircraft of no more than 15 seats, updating the legal rules, and promoting seaplane pilot projects such as Krabi–Phuket and Koh Lipe in Satun province, possibly allowing experienced foreign pilots on a temporary basis while developing Thai staff. It resolved that the secretariat gather the problems and proposals, and that operators send cost data so fees suited to aircraft size can be considered. For Phuket, the meeting followed transport projects because of heavy traffic, especially on Highway 402, which links Phuket airport with the south of the island. Key projects include widening Highway 4027 to 4 lanes, roads linking the airport and bypassing the Tha Ruea junction, the Kathu–Patong expressway (3.98 km), the Phuket airport–Ko Kaeo–Kathu expressway (30.62 km), and the Phuket mass transit (LRT) of about 42 km, whose model is under review with service planned for 2032. Some projects are held up by land-use permits, land expropriation and environmental impact assessment. The meeting proposed speeding up parallel roads, especially Highway 4027, and the expressways before large works on Highway 402, with a local follow-up mechanism. It noted the progress report.

Working group on small aircraft and seaplanes, and reports from the new subcommittees
se: Following meetings 23 and 24, the committee considered how the working group on aviation fees and seaplanes will work, focusing on reviewing take-off and landing fees and ground service charges to suit small aircraft, and linking routes to secondary cities and tourist spots. Operators and agencies will be invited to give information so that recommendations can be made to the Cabinet. The working group meets for the first time on 25 November 2026. The committee also heard progress from the new subcommittees, such as the one studying Andaman deep-sea ports as smart ports, which proposes developing them as a trade gateway, and the one studying the oversight of ride-hailing apps, which proposes, for example, QR codes to check drivers' records and better insurance and compensation for passengers.
